class="xcKE2u">The old North station</h3><div class="w4Ja51">Just past that knotted wooden cross
stands the old North station.

Across the highway, I spy:
   A leathery Bible-book of a man,
      his dark wrinkles
      eating up the sunlight,
      and grinning with delight
      as they multiply.
   The sun,
      it drives him onwards,
      showing our weary traveler
      the way, and
   his big walking stick
      thumps
      the ground around
   the old North station.

Coming through!
 
Now, he sits before it,
a sturdy wooden bench his throne.</div></section><a href="https://www.deviantart.com/jay1actually/art/The-old-North-station-1358392047" class="LBeGvY" aria-label="The old North station by jay1actually, literature"><span></span></a><div class="hjM2Ad zg9BI2" style="width:284px;height:284px" aria-hidden="true"><div class="F00MmM"><div class="J0GBVP Q7kSJx nBDkwL"></div></div><div class="XZcV56"><div style="width:284px;height:284px" class="ZE9aRP"><div class="QxGqXx"><div class="HqfGLS LAvrBA"><div class="OX5pSk"><div class="LpLuZV"></div><div class="Yq3_fn"></div></div></div><div class="Wek3HW"></div></div><div class="BTjvAm"></div><div class="hDT3Ic"><div class="HqfGLS"></div><div class="j0QN15 Wek3HW R2iuBb"></div></div></div></div><div class="pfPj_j XZcV56 theme-dark forced-theme-dark surface surface-primary" style="width:284px;height:284px"><div class="z5Z8UA"><div class="bWojeb"></div><div class="F00MmM nHbUOv"><div role="group" class="tuRfxI" data-anchor-id="_R_cbqq8uvli8q_" aria-describedby="tooltip-_R_cbqq8uvli8q_"><style>[data-anchor-id="_R_cbqq8uvli8q_"] { anchor-name: --anchor-tooltip-_R_cbqq8uvli8q_; }

"The Man Trap" saw the crew of the USS Enterprise encountering a mysterious space vampire on an alien planet. Funny thing about this episode? It wasn't even the actual pilot episode of Star Trek! After a failed first pilot episode was rejected as "too brainy" for audiences, a rare second pilot episode secured the show's future; but even that pilot wasn't aired until the third episode of season 1. "The Man Trap" won out as it featured distinct sci-fi elements, a mysterious alien monster, and showcase the main trio of Kirk, Spock, and McCoy. Who knew!
 
In honor of this stellar anniversary, I have a galaxy full of fun Star Trek facts, fictions, and fantasies for you to enjoy below. Set phasers for fun!

Nov 28, 2024 DeviantArt is proud to announce a new opportunity for deviants to contribute to the community at a deeper level! The Ambassador program is designed to give deviants a chance to bring artists together, offer ways for artists to hone their skills or try new things, and help shape the future of the community. Deviants eligible to participate in the Ambassador program are those who are co-founders or top contributors of official DeviantArt groups or affiliated groups. There are many factors that determine whether or not deviants might be a good fit for the Ambassador program, but all potential ambassadors should: Frequently run or organize community events Routinely be active participants in their community Consistently encourage and cheer on other artists Ambassadors will have direct contact with and support from DeviantArt team members when hosting events and challenges, to help their projects thrive. If you require legal advice, you should seek the services of a qualified attorney.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003E\\u003Cb\\u003EHow do I get Copyright?\\u003C\\u002Fb\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EUnder most national laws and international copyright treaties you receive a copyright automatically in any original work as you make it. Copyright protects the expression of ideas or the ways in which an idea is materially placed or expressed in the work.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003E\\u003Cb\\u003EWhat is Copyright Infringement?\\u003C\\u002Fb\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003ETo simplify this question, copyright infringement occurs when you do certain things with a creative work which someone else produced without first getting the proper permission.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003ESome examples of copyright infringement (this is only a partial listing) can include:\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cul\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EPlacing someone else\'s photograph or creative work online without proper permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EUsing a creative work commercially without permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EAdapting someone else\'s creative work found in one medium to another medium, such as making a book into a movie or a photograph into a painting.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EModifying or editing a creative work without proper permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Ful\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003E\\u003Cb\\u003EHow Can I Avoid Infringing on Someone\'s Copyright?\\u003C\\u002Fb\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EThe best way to avoid infringing on the rights of another creative person is to use your skill, talent and imagination to create your own completely original work. When we use the word \'original\' we don\'t mean that you must come up with an idea which hasn\'t been used before - recall that copyright does not protect ideas. When used in reference to copyright \\\"original\\\" means that you created your work without referencing or deliberately copying anyone else\'s work during the process.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EEnsure that all parts of your work, both visual and audio, are your own original creations. If you have used materials which are owned by other people or companies make certain that you have obtained proper permission or licensing for the use before you place your work online.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EYou can also obtain permission to use a copyrighted work by license. You can read more \\u003ClinkKbCopyright\\u003Ehere\\u003C\\u002FlinkKbCopyright\\u003E.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003E\\u003Cb\\u003EWhat Sort of Things are Copyrighted?\\u003C\\u002Fb\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EThe easy answer to this question is that just about any creative work that is less than 150 years old you might find should be considered copyrighted by default. \\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EA work is not required to have a copyright statement printed on it or near it in order to be considered copyrighted so do not assume that the work is unprotected simply because you cannot see a notice written anywhere.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EAlso do not confuse the fact that a work is publicly available with the idea that it is in the public domain or free for use. Being easy to find on the internet does not affect a work\'s copyrighted status.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EThere are many exceptions to the 150 year guideline, but you are best advised to obtain legal advice from an expert if you intend to rely on the possibility that a modern work is not copyrighted.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003E\\u003Cb\\u003ESome Cautions\\u003C\\u002Fb\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cul\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EIn most cases it does not matter how much of the material you have used, whether it\'s a single frame, a few moments of audio, a short clip of video or any other sampling it\'s still considered to be protected by copyright and you still require the owner\'s permission for use.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EIt doesn\'t matter how you obtained the material, it\'s still considered copyrighted and you still need permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EIt doesn\'t matter whether or not you\'ve credited the proper owner, it\'s still considered copyrighted and you still need permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EIt doesn\'t matter if you are not selling it or making a profit, it\'s still considered copyrighted and you still need permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EIt doesn\'t matter if you can find other people using things without permission, it\'s still considered copyrighted and you still need permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EIt doesn\'t matter if you\'ve edited it a little bit or made a few alterations, if it\'s recognizable it\'s still considered copyrighted and you still need permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003ERead licenses carefully to understand the type of permission they provide. starts, but that's only the beginning. We are the movement for the liberation of creative expression. We believe that art is for everyone, and we're creating the cultural context for how it is created, discovered, and shared.</p><img src="https://st.deviantart.net/minish/tour/fella_community_about.png?1" alt="Fella" style="float:right"/><p>Founded in August 2000, DeviantArt is the largest online social network for artists and art enthusiasts, and a platform for emerging and established artists to exhibit, promote, and share their works with an enthusiastic, art-centric community. We have over 100 million registered members worldwide and host over 650 million pieces of art on the platform. Our members -- known as deviants -- upload tens of thousands of original pieces of art every day, everything from painting and sculpture to digital art, pixel art, films, and anime.</p><p>Artists love us because we are an inclusive and supportive community. We help them find their identity through self-expression. We provide the tools, resources, and exposure to enable them to become better, more successful artists. We inspire people to create art by feeding their creativity. We can't help it - it runs through our veins and compels us to nurture it in others. This is DeviantArt.</p><h2>Meet The DeviantArt Staff</h2><p>Our team is made up of diverse and talented individuals from all over the world. We take great pride in creating a supportive environment for the online artist community. If you require legal advice, you should seek the services of a qualified attorney.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003E\\u003Cb\\u003EHow do I get Copyright?\\u003C\\u002Fb\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EUnder most national laws and international copyright treaties you receive a copyright automatically in any original work as you make it. Copyright protects the expression of ideas or the ways in which an idea is materially placed or expressed in the work.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003E\\u003Cb\\u003EWhat is Copyright Infringement?\\u003C\\u002Fb\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003ETo simplify this question, copyright infringement occurs when you do certain things with a creative work which someone else produced without first getting the proper permission.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003ESome examples of copyright infringement (this is only a partial listing) can include:\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cul\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EPlacing someone else\'s photograph or creative work online without proper permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EUsing a creative work commercially without permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EAdapting someone else\'s creative work found in one medium to another medium, such as making a book into a movie or a photograph into a painting.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EModifying or editing a creative work without proper permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Ful\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003E\\u003Cb\\u003EHow Can I Avoid Infringing on Someone\'s Copyright?\\u003C\\u002Fb\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EThe best way to avoid infringing on the rights of another creative person is to use your skill, talent and imagination to create your own completely original work. When we use the word \'original\' we don\'t mean that you must come up with an idea which hasn\'t been used before - recall that copyright does not protect ideas. When used in reference to copyright \\\"original\\\" means that you created your work without referencing or deliberately copying anyone else\'s work during the process.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EEnsure that all parts of your work, both visual and audio, are your own original creations. If you have used materials which are owned by other people or companies make certain that you have obtained proper permission or licensing for the use before you place your work online.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EYou can also obtain permission to use a copyrighted work by license. You can read more \\u003ClinkKbCopyright\\u003Ehere\\u003C\\u002FlinkKbCopyright\\u003E.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003E\\u003Cb\\u003EWhat Sort of Things are Copyrighted?\\u003C\\u002Fb\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EThe easy answer to this question is that just about any creative work that is less than 150 years old you might find should be considered copyrighted by default. \\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EA work is not required to have a copyright statement printed on it or near it in order to be considered copyrighted so do not assume that the work is unprotected simply because you cannot see a notice written anywhere.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EAlso do not confuse the fact that a work is publicly available with the idea that it is in the public domain or free for use. Being easy to find on the internet does not affect a work\'s copyrighted status.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003EThere are many exceptions to the 150 year guideline, but you are best advised to obtain legal advice from an expert if you intend to rely on the possibility that a modern work is not copyrighted.\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cp\\u003E\\u003Cb\\u003ESome Cautions\\u003C\\u002Fb\\u003E\\u003C\\u002Fp\\u003E\\u003Cul\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EIn most cases it does not matter how much of the material you have used, whether it\'s a single frame, a few moments of audio, a short clip of video or any other sampling it\'s still considered to be protected by copyright and you still require the owner\'s permission for use.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EIt doesn\'t matter how you obtained the material, it\'s still considered copyrighted and you still need permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EIt doesn\'t matter whether or not you\'ve credited the proper owner, it\'s still considered copyrighted and you still need permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EIt doesn\'t matter if you are not selling it or making a profit, it\'s still considered copyrighted and you still need permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EIt doesn\'t matter if you can find other people using things without permission, it\'s still considered copyrighted and you still need permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003EIt doesn\'t matter if you\'ve edited it a little bit or made a few alterations, if it\'s recognizable it\'s still considered copyrighted and you still need permission.\\u003C\\u002Fli\\u003E\\u003Cli\\u003ERead licenses carefully to understand the type of permission they provide. Advertise with us Contact us Help & FAQ Community etiquette policy Accessibility statement Bleed and Breed Art ™ We are where art starts, but that's only the beginning. We are the movement for the liberation of creative expression. We believe that art is for everyone, and we're creating the cultural context for how it is created, discovered, and shared. Founded in August 2000, DeviantArt is the largest online social network for artists and art enthusiasts, and a platform for emerging and established artists to exhibit, promote, and share their works with an enthusiastic, art-centric community. We have over 100 million registered members worldwide and host over 650 million pieces of art on the platform. Our members -- known as deviants -- upload tens of thousands of original pieces of art every day, everything from painting and sculpture to digital art, pixel art, films, and anime. Artists love us because we are an inclusive and supportive community. We help them find their identity through self-expression. We provide the tools, resources, and exposure to enable them to become better, more successful artists. We inspire people to create art by feeding their creativity. We can't help it - it runs through our veins and compels us to nurture it in others. This is DeviantArt. Meet The DeviantArt Staff Our team is made up of diverse and talented individuals from all over the world. We take great pride in creating a supportive environment for the online artist community. You can find us around the site by looking for the symbol after our usernames. And we're not just staff members - we're artists too. Live long and prosper because it's Star Trek Day! 60 years ago today, on September 8th 1966, the first episode of Star Trek aired in the United States of America. "The Man Trap" saw the crew of the USS Enterprise encountering a mysterious space vampire on an alien planet. Funny thing about this episode? It wasn't even the actual pilot episode of Star Trek! After a failed first pilot episode was rejected as "too brainy" for audiences, a rare second pilot episode secured the show's future; but even that pilot wasn't aired until the third episode of season 1. "The Man Trap" won out as it featured distinct sci-fi elements, a mysterious alien monster, and showcase the main trio of Kirk, Spock, and McCoy. Who knew!
 
In honor of this stellar anniversary, I have a galaxy full of fun Star Trek facts, fictions, and fantasies for you to enjoy below. Set phasers for fun!

class="">Aug 5, 2026</time></div><div class="A9rGzI">Hello everyone,

[GIF]

I am known as Malintra-Shadowmoon (friends call me Mali): I live in Germany and have been a Community Volunteer (CV) for over six years. I received my first CV role in Literature in April 2020, shortly after earning my Senior Medal in January of that same year. Later, I added Artisan Crafts and Traditional Art to my responsibilities. Following the introduction of AI on DA, I strongly advocated for Synthography/AI to have its own category and become eligible for Daily Deviations (DDs). As this was important to me, I was delighted to become one of the first CVs for this category.

[EMOTE]    [EMOTE]     [EMOTE]     [EMOTE][EMOTE]

My journey on DA began about 14 years ago, in April 2012. At the time, I wasn't sure whether to join Elfwood Lysator (which has long since ceased to exist) or DA. I felt that literature was more highly valued on DA than on Elfwood, I fortunately chose DA—and I couldn't have wished for a better home for my art.

"The Man Trap" saw the crew of the USS Enterprise encountering a mysterious space vampire on an alien planet. Funny thing about this episode? It wasn't even the actual pilot episode of Star Trek! After a failed first pilot episode was rejected as "too brainy" for audiences, a rare second pilot episode secured the show's future; but even that pilot wasn't aired until the third episode of season 1. "The Man Trap" won out as it featured distinct sci-fi elements, a mysterious alien monster, and showcase the main trio of Kirk, Spock, and McCoy. Who knew! In honor of this stellar anniversary, I have a galaxy full of fun Star Trek facts, fictions, and fantasies for you to enjoy below. Set phasers for fun!
